newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister, back from Mideast, sees distrust.
newsitem.headline: French minister, back from Mideast, sees distrust.

text.p: French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette, back from a trip to the Middle East, said on Sunday that distrust now prevailed in the region where a year ago all parties believed peace was within reach.

"A year ago, before the elections in Israel and before the Lebanese tragedy, the whole world and those chiefly concerned -- the Israelis, the Palestinians, the Syrians -- thought that peace was within reach.

"But today, trust has disappeared and on all sides people mistrust each other," De Charette told France-3 in an interview after visiting Syria, Israel and Lebanon in a French drive to carve itself more influence in the region.
Asked whether the Israelis were to blame for trying to dictate the terms of the peace process with U.S. support, De Charette answered:
"It's true that there are highs and lows in the attitude of the new Israeli government. I would say the Hebron accord was good news and since then there have been incidents, difficulties."

Israel handed over most of the West Bank town of Hebron to Palestinian rule in January but has angered Palestinians with a unilateral decision on Friday on a further troop withdrawal that they say is insufficient and a violation of peace accords.
